The problem with this theory is that all of the emotions listed are base emotions, all of them interchangeable with eachother. Confusion can lead to hatred, hatred can lead to anger, anger to hate and so on.

The proposed physical close off of the body when suppressed by emotional turmoil is a falsehood, the body needs to be told when to do something and also when to stop doing it. It's a system that requires both push and pull. If you close yourself off so much that physical deterioration occurs then you're in a coma or dead, not emotionally numb.

A lot of the force ethos is based around the idea of notion, the mastery of mind where a notion is strongly projected onto physical space with a little deviation from a singular clear notion. The dark side of the force ignores this clarity, if their use of the force can be amplified by disregarding the distinct nature of their notion, how it is seperated from other physicallities, then they will exploit that.

The reason the jedi are so against this practise is that it has fallout, lifting a rock and moving it across a room while keeping careful control of your clarity of mind and the distinct nature of the rock means you will cleanly lift the rock and move it. A dark side user would tear up the floor and wall in their emotion driven understanding of the rock and it's physical resistance to their need for it to move and then toss it across the room in a single notion, disragarding any control of their self or the rock in favour of speed and, most importantly, power.

That's why the dark side is often a force to be feared even when in a minority, it can often outclass light side usage even with the same training. But it is also destructive to it's surroundings and inherently self destructive to it's users as they reach for greater and greater emotional fervour they lose the ability to feel less powerful emotions as their brain is hardwiring itself to large scale input. This creates a disconnect for dark side users from normal people, they don't understand the petty emotions and worries of people who haven't scoured their mind with constant outbursts of effort and satisfaction.

Jedis struggle with this as well, but from the opposite end of the scale. A jedi begins to see people who don't maintain a cool neutrality to their mind, those who allow emotional input to impact their clarity of thought to be less in control and thus less able. If jedis were to be as inherently power hungry as sith then the universe would be a bleak place full of emotionless goverments with little to no debate as efficiency and conformity stand above all other factors. But the fact that dominance is an emotional attraction makes jedi isolationist, they seek to deistance themselves from those who might influence them with emotion and disturb their meditative life.

It seems like Lucas wanted Sith to represent the masculine warrior archetype while Jedi are more matriarchal, or mystical, since this same divergence plays out in differences between western religions which focus on apocalyptic change while eastern ways of thinking such as Buddhism tend to focus more on harmony or keeping things in a balanced sate. These same archetypes are flipped in politics since conservatives, who like receiving wisdom from the past for informing the future, tend to express a masculine archetype while many leftists, from my viewpoint, convey a more feminine archetype through change or progressivism.
